note: Hand-picked recent AI reporting from large, reputable newsrooms, links verified. Source mix is limited by access tooling: WSJ, Reuters, FT and Bloomberg are blocked from automated browsing, so the openable/verified set skews CNBC, AP (wire) and MIT Technology Review. The updater (8×/day) can broaden sources over time.

items.title: King Charles to press Nvidia, OpenAI, Anthropic leaders on AI safety at summit
items.blurb: Royal summit convenes senior AI executives Thursday on shared development principles, adding another venue to the week's safety-versus-speed debate.

items.title: OpenAI and Anthropic are making 10 times more revenue than all Chinese AI models combined, research group Rhodium says
items.blurb: Rhodium estimates China's AI models collectively earn about a tenth of the two US leaders' revenue, despite strong open-weight adoption.

items.title: AI needs to have 'reasonable guidelines,' Palantir's Karp tells CNBC
items.blurb: Palantir CEO calls for enforced AI guidelines and floats nationalization as regulation debate intensifies among industry leaders.

items.title: AI's imminent hacking threat is hiding in plain sight
items.blurb: Executives and former officials warn automated AI cyberattacks on grids and vehicles are nearer than doomsday scenarios suggest.

items.title: OpenAI investors have approached the company about a new funding round
items.blurb: Investors are courting OpenAI for a fresh round ahead of its expected 2027 IPO; prospectus confidentially filed in June.

items.title: China's AI leaders keep quiet despite U.S. 'publicity' on tech risks
items.blurb: Z.ai, Moonshot, MiniMax, Alibaba and Tencent decline to echo U.S. labs' safety warnings, focusing on applications instead.

items.title: CNBC Daily Open: Is AI safe? Industry leaders and Trump disagree
items.blurb: OpenAI, Anthropic and Google convene on safety while Trump keeps attacking slowdown advocates; the standoff hardens.

items.title: An aging Congress' dilemma: Can they regulate AI without using it?
items.blurb: Over two dozen lawmakers pressed to regulate AI admit they rarely or never use it, raising competence questions.

items.title: Google, Nvidia and Emerald AI launch flexible data center power coalition
items.blurb: Twenty companies including Anthropic back data centers that flex power demand to curb electricity prices and ease grid strain.

items.title: Google, DeepMind launch institute to explore AGI
items.blurb: New forum for Google, DeepMind and outside researchers on AGI's societal impacts, opening with economics and transparency papers.

items.title: OpenAI reports 6 new instances of 'concerning model behavior' since March
items.blurb: OpenAI discloses six behavior incidents over six months and a new framework for reporting future model misbehavior.

items.title: Arm CEO says he's more confident its new AI chip can meet a loftier $2B revenue goal
items.blurb: Rene Haas says Arm's new data-center CPU is tracking toward Wall Street's raised revenue expectations.

items.title: Building the materials foundation for AI
items.blurb: Semiconductors and data centers near physical limits on heat and efficiency, making advanced materials a compute-buildout bottleneck.

items.title: Anthropic, OpenAI proposed new 'neutral' AI watchdogs. Why you should worry about the idea
items.blurb: Labs float third-party oversight bodies; critics question independence of watchdogs the industry itself would help design and fund.

items.title: Scoop: U.S. open to discuss AI "shared risks" with China, Bessent says
items.blurb: Treasury signals willingness to discuss AI risk with Beijing, covering both open and closed-weight models — a notable de-escalation signal.

items.title: House votes to curb AI data center costs
items.blurb: Bipartisan 417-3 bill pushes state regulators to make data centers cover new power-generation costs, shielding household bills.

items.title: Media execs sound alarm on AI
items.blurb: Print, digital, and broadcast leaders call LLM training on journalism unprecedented IP theft, escalating the publisher-lab standoff.

items.title: CNBC Daily Open: Beware AI naysayers, the 'Hoax Buster' is here
items.blurb: Trump doubles down against AI-risk warnings as markets steady, keeping Washington split on the slowdown push.

items.title: "I am the Hoax Buster": Trump's war on AI doomers gets personal
items.blurb: Trump escalates against slowdown advocates, calling extinction warnings a conspiracy, phoning into Huang's All-In Summit interview live.

items.title: Why a swift AI pause is unlikely: No one trusts AI companies
items.blurb: Mutual distrust among labs, rivals and Washington makes the CEOs' proposed coordinated slowdown hard to actually execute.

items.title: Trump's opposition to AI rules undercuts industry's calls for a slowdown
items.blurb: The president's refusal to back any AI regulation leaves the labs' slowdown plan without a federal enforcement path.

items.title: AI models need more data about biology, and OpenAI is paying to create it
items.blurb: OpenAI Foundation funds high-quality biology datasets to push AI in medicine, part of a $1B giveaway this year.

items.title: Wall Street weighs prospect of an AI slowdown on data center buildout
items.blurb: Investors begin pricing what a safety-driven slowdown would do to companies tied to the data-center buildout.

items.title: Private sector is 'the right place' to solve AI threats, White House's Hassett says
items.blurb: Top Trump economic adviser rejects government-led AI regulation days after lab CEOs asked for a slowdown.
